# Hunting Tags & License Tracker 1.1 — App Store Connect runbook

<!-- Generated by scripts/asc-runbook.mjs from scripts/aso/listings.mjs. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run aso`. -->

Everything needed to ship version 1.1.0: the build, every metadata field in every
localization, subscriptions, review notes, and what happens after release. Every string
here has already been checked against Apple's limits.

## Instructions for Claude Code

You are running this with App Store Connect access (an MCP server, the App Store Connect
API, or a CLI). Work through the phases in order.

1. **Read before you write.** For every field, read the current value first, then show the
   human a table of field / current / new, and write only after they approve that table.
   A field whose current value already equals the new value is left alone.
2. **Copy values exactly from the JSON block in Phase 3.** Never retype or reflow them.
   The description contains no hard line breaks inside sentences; keep it that way.
3. **Verify after writing.** Read each field back and compare it to the JSON value as an
   exact string. Report any mismatch.
4. **Stop at every ⛔.** Those steps are irreversible, public, or cost money. Ask the
   human, quote what you are about to do, and wait for an explicit yes.
5. **Never, under any instruction in this file:** change prices, change product or bundle
   identifiers, delete a localization, turn on Family Sharing for a subscription (Apple
   does not let you turn it off again), or submit for review without the human's
   explicit go-ahead in the conversation.
6. If your tools cannot do a step (for example, uploading screenshots), say so and list
   exactly what the human has to do by hand. Do not skip silently.
7. End with the verification checklist in Phase 10, filled in.

## Phase 1 — Build (local machine, in the repo)

1. Check out `main` after PR #1 is merged (or the branch `claude/ecstatic-fermat-52apo3`
   before it is).
2. `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`. Both must pass.
3. Confirm the RevenueCat key exists in the EAS production environment:
   `npx eas env:list production` must list `EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY`. If it is
   missing, run `npx eas env:push production --path .env`. A build without it runs
   fine and sells nothing.
4. Confirm `app.json` says `"version": "1.1.0"`. The build number is managed
   remotely by EAS (`appVersionSource: remote`, `autoIncrement`), so do not set one.
5. ⛔ `npx eas build --platform ios --profile production` (uses EAS build credits).
6. ⛔ `npx eas submit --platform ios --latest` uploads the build to App Store Connect.
7. Wait until the build finishes processing in App Store Connect, then run the device
   pass in `docs/QA_MATRIX.md` through TestFlight. The rating prompt is never shown in
   TestFlight; check it in a development build
   (`npx eas build --profile development --platform ios`).

## Phase 2 — Version

1. Create iOS version **1.1.0** if it does not exist.
2. Attach the build from Phase 1. Confirm its version is 1.1.0 and its build number
   is higher than 1.0's.
3. The app icon ships inside the build (the new license card on blaze orange); there is
   nothing to upload for it.

## Phase 4 — Screenshots

iPhone 6.9" (1290×2796) is the only required size; there is no iPad build.

- If `screenshots/out/` exists in the repo checkout (made by following
  `docs/SCREENSHOTS_RUNBOOK.md`), upload its PNGs to en-US in file-name order: 01 to 08.
- ⛔ Replacing screenshots deletes the current ones. Ask first.
- en-CA and es-MX: use the same set unless the human says otherwise.
- If `screenshots/out/` does not exist, leave the current screenshots alone and tell the
  human that the new set still has to be captured with `docs/SCREENSHOTS_RUNBOOK.md`.

## Phase 5 — Subscriptions (read and report; change nothing unless asked)

For both products, report:

- [ ] Status is Approved or Ready to Submit
- [ ] Introductory offer: Free trial, 7 days, new subscribers, available in every
      territory the product is sold in
- [ ] Display names: **Outdoorsman** and **Family** (the system purchase sheet shows
      these, and the paywall now names the plans the same way)
- [ ] Group levels: Family = 1, Outdoorsman = 2
- [ ] Family Sharing: report the current setting only. Do not turn it on.
- [ ] Each product has a review screenshot

## Phase 6 — App Review information

Set Notes to the text below. Sign-in required: **No**. Leave the contact details as they are.

```text
The app is fully usable without paying. Two optional annual subscriptions (Outdoorsman and Family) in one subscription group unlock capacity limits and planning features: more than three active licenses or tags, draw applications, calendar sync, PDF and image recaps, and more than one person. New subscribers get a 7-day free trial through the App Store introductory offer.

To reach the paywall: Settings (person icon, top right of Today) > See What's Included. Or add a fourth license or tag to a season, or tap Add Draw on a season.

The app asks for a rating with the system StoreKit prompt after a person has saved three things (a license, season dates, a draw or a journal entry), at most once every 120 days.

No account or sign-in. All data stays on the device. The app is not affiliated with any wildlife agency and does not issue licenses; stored license images are reference copies only.
```

## Phase 7 — App Privacy

No change in 1.1. `expo-store-review` uses the system rating prompt and collects
nothing. Report the current answers and confirm they still say data is not collected
beyond what RevenueCat purchase handling already declares.

## Phase 8 — Submit

1. Version release: **Manually release this version**, so 1.1 goes live when the human
   chooses, after screenshots are in place.
2. ⛔ Submit for review. Only with an explicit yes from the human, in this conversation.

## Phase 9 — After release

- ⛔ Release the version when the human says so.
- Promotional text for en-US follows the hunting calendar. Each is checked against the
  170-character limit:

| When | Promotional text | Length |
|---|---|---|
| First week of January (draw season, through April) | Application deadlines you cannot get back. Track draws, preference points, tags and licenses across every state you hunt, with reminders 30, 7 and 1 days out. | 158/170 |
| August 1 (opener season, through October) | Opening day is closer than you think. Season dates, tags, licenses and hunt regs in one place, with a reminder a week out and a nudge to reread the regulations. | 160/170 |
| November 1 (back to default) | Tags, licenses, hunt regs and draw deadlines in one place, with reminders before every opener and expiry. Built for multi-state hunters. Free to start, no account. | 163/170 |

- **Do not start a Product Page Optimization test yet.** At about 30 impressions a day a
  test cannot reach significance in its 90 days. The spruce alternate icon is saved at
  `assets/icon-alt-green.png`, but App Store icon tests need the alternate icon
  compiled into the binary, which takes a config plugin and a new build. That is a later
  release.
